[Docs](https://www.quantummetric.com/docs)

## Overview

The Quantum Metric MCP Server connects your Quantum Metric subscription to AI assistants and automated systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard for giving AI tools structured access to external systems.

Once connected, an AI client can query behavioral data, investigate sessions and errors, run funnels and saved queries, and trigger the workflows and Background Agents you have built in Quantum Metric.

This guide covers integration tokens: credentials that let an automated system call Quantum Metric MCP with no person present. Use them for scheduled analysis, experiment read-outs, automated remediation and agent frameworks.

## What an integration token is

An integration token is a credential for your subscription. Your automation sends it with every request.

| Property | Integration token |
| Acts as | A service account for your subscription |
| Set up by | Quantum Metric |
| Lifetime | Until it is revoked |
| Workspace and timezone | None bound by default; set per call |

## Before you begin

You need:

- An active Quantum Metric subscription.
- Your subscription name, as it appears in your Quantum Metric URL.
- An MCP-capable client: Claude Code, Claude (desktop and web), ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, or any client that implements MCP.

## Endpoint

There is one production endpoint, with your subscription in the path:

```
https://api.quantummetric.com/mcp/<subscription>
```

Replace `<subscription>` with your subscription name.

## Getting an integration token

MCP tokens are created by Quantum Metric. Talk to your Customer Success representative to get one for your subscription.

## Connect with an integration token

Send the token as a bearer credential to the endpoint with your subscription in the path.

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-integration-token>
```

**Claude Code:**

```
claude mcp add --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer <your-integration-token>" felix https://api.quantummetric.com/mcp/<subscription>
```

**Clients that take JSON configuration:**

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "felix": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.quantummetric.com/mcp/<subscription>",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <your-integration-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Note: If you get a 400 error, ensure you are sending with the correct subscription.

## Verify the connection

1. In Claude Code, run `claude mcp list`. The `felix` server should show as connected. Other clients show connection status in their MCP or connector settings.
2. Ask a question that needs your data, such as "List the dashboards in this subscription."
3. Call `get_context` and confirm the subscription is the one you expect.

## Set your workspace and timezone on every call

A token session has no user profile, so it has no default workspace and runs in UTC. Pass both values on every call.

- **Workspace is required.** Team workspaces, and any segment attached to them, scope what a query sees. A data call without `workspace` fails with `Error: no workspace set. Pass the workspace parameter (list_workspaces shows the options).`
- **Timezone defaults to UTC.** Pass `timezone` as an IANA name, such as `America/New_York`, so "yesterday" and daily breakdowns line up with your business day.

If automated numbers disagree with numbers a colleague pulled in the Quantum Metric UI, compare the workspace and timezone first. The UI uses their workspace and their own timezone.

**Step 1: find the workspace ID.** Call `list_workspaces`; it returns each workspace's `id` and `name`. Or resolve a name directly:

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "switch_workspace",
    "arguments": { "workspace": "Checkout Team" }
  }
}
```

The reply gives the exact `workspace` value to pass. It changes nothing on the server.

**Step 2: pass**`workspace` **and**`timezone` **on each call.** For example, a `run_query` call:

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "run_query",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "Conversion rate by device type",
      "time_phrase": "yesterday",
      "workspace": "<workspace-id>",
      "timezone": "America/New_York"
    }
  }
}
```

The same two arguments work on `run_saved_query`, `run_funnel`, `execute_dashboard_card` and the other data tools. `create_saved_query` is the exception: it takes `workspace_id`.

**If an AI agent makes the calls,** put the values in its instructions, for example:

```
On every Felix tool call that accepts them, pass workspace: "<workspace-id>" and timezone: "America/New_York".
```

**Step 3: check what answered.** Workspace-scoped responses echo the workspace that answered. `run_saved_query` also returns `workspace_id`, `workspace_name` and `workspace_filter_applied`.

## Building autonomous workflows

An integration token makes calls as your subscription's service account. The automation's access does not depend on any person's session or employment.

### Know what each call does

| Kind | Tools | What to know |
| Read | Nearly all tools | Return data. No state changes. |
| Create | `create_saved_query` | Saves a new saved query in your subscription. |
| Invoke | `run_monitoring_agent`, `execute_workflow` | Run an agent or workflow saved in Felix. Its side effects are whatever its author configured: notifications, deliveries, downstream actions. |

Before you put an invoke tool in an unattended loop, confirm what that agent or workflow does when it runs.

### Confirm your scope

- `run_saved_query` returns a context block with `workspace_id`, `workspace_name` and `workspace_filter_applied`. `workspace_filter_applied: false` means the workspace has no segment filter; the workspace still applies.
- To confirm empirically, count a value your workspace segment excludes in All Traffic and in the workspace, and compare.

### Handle failures by status code

- **400:** configuration error in the URL. Retrying will not fix it.
- **401:** credential problem. Check the token value and replace it if revoked.
- **403:** the token is valid but missing Felix MCP access. Alert a person; retrying will not fix it.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| Client connects, but no tools appear | The client loads MCP configuration only at startup | Restart the client. Confirm the URL is `https://api.quantummetric.com/mcp/<subscription>`. |
| 400, message about a missing subscription | Token sent to a URL with no subscription in the path | Add your subscription to the URL. |
| 401 invalid token | Token value mistyped or revoked. | Copy the token value again from Integration Settings. |
| 403, token lacks the felix\_mcp scope | Token created without Felix MCP ticked | Ask your Customer Success contact to turn on Felix MCP for the token. Wait a minute before retrying. |
| Browser login opens when using a token | The Authorization header was not sent | Re-add the server with the header. |
| Results differ from the Quantum Metric UI | Different workspace, or the call ran in UTC | Run `get_context`; pass `workspace` and `timezone` on each call. |
| "Error: no workspace set" | Token sessions have no default workspace | Pass `workspace` with an ID from `list_workspaces`. |
| Unrecognized parameter | Tools reject parameters they do not define | Check the name against the tool definition, e.g. `workspace`, not `workspace_id`. |
| Query times out | Analytics queries are limited to 120 seconds | Narrow the time range, add filters, or use a saved query. |
| Query returns no data | Wrong workspace, time range or event name | Confirm workspace, time range in the session timezone, and that the events exist. |

## Getting help

Contact your Customer Success Engineer for help connecting MCP to your systems or enabling token access settings.

## Appendix: tool reference

The server typically exposes tools across 16 capability areas. The list may change as the product develops; your client retrieves the current list at connect time. Some per-subscription tools, such as Voice of Customer survey tools, are unavailable to integration tokens.

A tool call is one authenticated tools/call request to the Quantum Metric MCP server.

| Area | What it covers |
| Workspaces | List team workspaces and resolve one to its ID |
| Context | Subscription, workspace, timezone and profile for the session |
| Analytics | Ad-hoc queries of behavioral and performance data |
| Saved Queries | List, run and create saved queries |
| Sessions and users | Session and user summaries, replay URLs, page hits, replay screenshots |
| Business Concepts | The business concept model configured for the subscription |
| Events | Event definitions, event discovery and event value search |
| Catalog | Metrics and dimensions available to query |
| Dashboards | List and inspect dashboards; run individual cards |
| The Quad | Search and read Quantum Metric knowledge base articles |
| Knowledge | Analytics skills and guidance available to the assistant |
| Page Discovery | Resolve a page name to an analytics filter |
| Funnels | List and run funnels; analyze step drop-off |
| Background Agents | List and run background agents; read results |
| Workflows | List and run workflows; read runs and reports |
| Alerts | Alerts, incidents, time series and affected sessions |
